transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Li (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (CTO - Kepler), Priya Shah (ML Engineer), Daniel Park (Eng Mgr)

Summary: Discovery call to understand Kepler's current embeddings + rerank architecture, vector DB choices, throughput requirements, storage/dimensionality constraints, and fit for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer focused on hybrid search (BM25 + dense), reranking options, and enterprise security (VPC, audit logs).

Topics: vector DB integration, throughput targets, embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536), hybrid search architecture, reranking with cross-encoders/LLM, Dedicated capacity sizing, private networking (VPC/VPN), SOC2/KMS.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Maya, AE on the west coast, and Jonah's our solutions engineer. you all good to go?
[00:06] Alex (CTO): Yep, thanks, Maya. Alex here. Priya and Daniel also on. we'll mainly talk about embeddings and rerank - high level + technical.
[00:12] Jonah (SE): Awesome. Can you give a quick run through of your current stack and pain points?
[00:16] Priya (ML): Sure. we're running a hybrid search today - Elastic for BM25 and Pinecone for dense. it's been ok but cost is creeping and latency spikes during peak. our rerank is a cross-encoder hosted on a GPU node that we call out to per top-k.
[00:28] Daniel (Eng Mgr): We saw big infra variability during campaigns - qps jumps from 200 to 1.2k. so we need predictable latency and cost.
[00:36] Jonah (SE): Got it. are you open to consolidating to a single pipeline or keep hybrid?
[00:40] Priya (ML): We want hybrid for exact recall on older docs but would love to move dense to something cheaper and more predictable. also curious about embedding dims - we generate 1536 dims from our current model but wonder if 768 would be ok.
[00:52] Maya (AE): Ok. Redwood supports Hosted and Dedicated. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, private gives VPC/on-prem. for your QPS and rerank pattern, Dedicated or Private would likely fit.
[01:04] Alex (CTO): Can we dig into throughput? indexing throughput and query qps, and reranking latency?
[01:09] Jonah (SE): Sure. what's your target p95 latency for a user-facing search?
[01:12] Daniel (Eng Mgr): Want under 150ms p95 for the initial recall path, reranker can be up to 400-500ms for the top-10 if needed. but ideally rerank <250ms.
[01:22] Jonah (SE): Ok. with Dedicated, we can route recall to a vector DB (we integrate with Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate or self-hosted) and run batching + prefix cache to reduce cost. typical pattern: dense recall in 20-50ms, then cross-encoder rerank on GPU - depending on model size that's 150-300ms per batch. we also do smart routing to fallback to lower-dimension models when busy.
[01:40] Priya (ML): you said fallback to lower-dimension models - how does that interact with our embeddings? we don't want quality cliffs.
[01:45] Jonah (SE): Good question. fallback is version-based: you can pin model versions and Redwood can route to a quantized/768-dim variant. the platform includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets so regressions trigger alerts.
[01:56] Alex (CTO): about vector DB integration - we mostly use Pinecone now. can Redwood host the embeddings and handle vector storage? we worry about data residency and egress costs.
[02:04] Maya (AE): Hosted stores embeddings in our managed service; Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and you can opt for Private where embeddings never leave your VPC or on-prem. for egress, Dedicated with VPC peering or Private on VPC avoids public egress - we'll include the network diagrams in the docs.
[02:18] Daniel (Eng Mgr): what about index size? we're planning ~10M docs to start, average doc embedding 1536 dims float32. storage and nearest neighbor performance matters.
[02:27] Jonah (SE): For 10M x 1536 float32 raw that's sizable. many customers use quantization (8-bit or product quantization) and IVF/HNSW indexes to reduce footprint. our Dedicated configs include GPUs for rerank and CPU nodes for index serving with sharding. we can share sizing tables - e.g., 10M at 1536 with PQ reduces storage ~4-8x depending on config.
[02:47] Priya (ML): does Redwood integrate directly with Milvus or would we have to proxy through your control plane?
[02:51] Jonah (SE): We have connectors for common vector DBs and can also host the vector index in Redwood Dedicated. if you prefer Milvus self-hosted in your VPC, we can do private control plane only and connect via peering.
[03:02] Alex (CTO): Rerank - our cross-encoder is a 110M-300M param model. can you run that as part of the pipeline or do we need separate infra?
[03:09] Jonah (SE): You can bring your own model or use Redwood-hosted variants. For 110M models, single GPU nodes handle batches of top-k efficiently. for larger models, we recommend batching and dynamic batching to amortize latency. Redwood Optimize gives batching recommendations per workload.
[03:24] Priya (ML): what about dimensionality tradeoffs? if we move from 1536 -> 768 we save cost but do we lose much in recall?
[03:30] Jonah (SE): It depends on your model and dataset. we typically run an evaluation harness - sample queries and nDCG comparisons - to quantify the drop. often moving to 1024 or using a distilled embedder keeps most signal. we can run a quick eval in the POC.
[03:44] Daniel (Eng Mgr): Security and compliance - we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS integration, audit logs. are those available?
[03:50] Maya (AE): Yes - Dedicated & Private support SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM, and full audit logs. Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem. we'll send SOC2 + network diagrams.
[04:01] Alex (CTO): Cost model - show us ballpark on Hosted vs Dedicated for stable baseline QPS ~500 and spikes to 1.2k.
[04:08] Maya (AE): We'll include a cost comparison in the pricing sheet. high-level: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, easier to start; Dedicated has a monthly commitment but reduces per-token/embedding cost and gives latency predictability. for your spikes, Dedicated with autoscaling/burst lanes is common.
[04:22] Priya (ML): POC plan - we'd like a 1-week run indexing our 10M sample, run 500-1.2k qps replay, and measure p50/p95 and cost.
[04:29] Jonah (SE): Perfect. we'll draft a POC test plan: index throughput, qps replay, top-k recall, rerank latency, and failure scenarios.
[04:36] crosstalk briefly as participants check calendars
[04:40] Daniel (Eng Mgr): timeline - we want POC in the next 2-3 weeks.
[04:44] Maya (AE): We'll aim to kick off within two weeks; I can send dates after this call.
[04:48] Alex (CTO): any blockers around data privacy? we have PII in some docs.
[04:52] Jonah (SE): We support field-level encryption, private deployments, and bring-your-own-key for embeddings. we'll flag data handling in the POC plan.
[05:02] Priya (ML): what's the normal indexing throughput we should expect? we need to get 10M docs in under 48 hours ideally.
[05:09] Jonah (SE): With bulk loaders and parallel indexing on Dedicated, 10M can be done in 12-36 hours depending on doc size and transform. we'll size nodes accordingly.
[05:20] Alex (CTO): Any gotchas around hybrid search and consistency? we want near-real-time updates when docs are updated.
[05:26] Jonah (SE): For near-RT, we recommend an append-only index plus background re-ingestion for heavy edits. Dedicated config supports low-latency upserts; we can tune tradeoffs for your SLA.
[05:38] Priya (ML): ok thanks. last question: rerank approach - do people use LLMs for rerank or cross-encoders? pros/cons?
[05:45] Jonah (SE): Cross-encoders are cheaper and deterministic for rerank. LLM rerank gives higher semantic quality and explainability but costs more and has variance. many customers use cross-encoder first pass, and optionally an LLM-check for special queries. Redwood supports both and can fall back when capacity is low.
[06:02] Maya (AE): Great - recap and next steps?
[06:05] Alex (CTO): recap: send pricing + diagrams, POC plan, security docs.
[06:09] Maya (AE): Yep. we'll send Dedicated pricing, SOC2 + network/VPC docs, and Jonah will send the POC test plan. Priya to share sample dataset and qps profile. Daniel to confirm stakeholders.
[06:18] Alex (CTO): thanks everyone. we'll look out for the docs.
[06:21] Maya (AE): Thanks - end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' / 'Pine-con'), some filler words removed for readability. References: shared deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/kepler-poc), POC spreadsheet (link: sent after call).
